jess (arch): quick heads-up — tenant alias churn is triggering eviction storms in staging again. we need a model for alias stability that avoids whole-shard evicts when a few tenants flip aliases.
liam (infra): can you sketch the failure mode? is this client-resolver churn or control-plane writes?
jess (arch): mostly control-plane alias updates during rapid rollouts + some client retry flapping. current behavior: alias write -> publish -> runtime evicts variant bindings immediately -> mass cold-starts.
nora (product): that's what broke several internal apps last week, pages spiked. users expect seamless canaries.
samir (runtime): eviction is cheap if just TTL, but cold-starts and cache rebuilds kill latency SLOs. we should avoid synchronous global evicts. maybe soft-unbind semantics?
jess (arch): proposal sketch: introduce rollout metadata fields to guide runtime eviction and client resolver: `stability_window_ms`, `evict_grace_ms`, `alias_mode` (values: hard, soft, sticky), and `client_probe_hint`. Example: 
```
{
  "rollout_id": "rl-20260323-42",
  "stability_window_ms": 600000,       // treat rapid flips within 10m as noisy
  "evict_grace_ms": 300000,           // delay hard eviction to let reuse happen
  "alias_mode": "soft",              // don't immediately unbind cached KV; mark as stale
  "client_probe_hint": "prefer-stable-variant" // resolver hint to avoid bouncing
}
```
liam (infra): how does this interact with tenant-scoped pinning? tenants can still explicitly pin a version — do pins override soft mode?
jess (arch): explicit tenant pins must always win. soft mode only applies to non-pinned aliases and rollout-driven automatic switches.
vlad (sre): we need metrics and tracing hooks: `alias_transition_count`, `deferred_eviction_seconds`, `pin_overrides_count`. also an alert for sustained deferred_eviction > configured SLO.
samir (runtime): implementation notes: runtime should maintain a lease state for alias entries: (active, pending-deferred-evict, stale). when alias flips, mark previous as pending-deferred-evict and start a background reconcile. only promote to hard-evict after evict_grace_ms and low traffic. this avoids thundering cold starts.
nora (product): UX question — will customers see potential dual-serving during grace window? we need to surface behavior in docs and console. maybe a rollout timeline in console UI.
jess (arch): yep — add `expected_dual_serve` flag to metadata and surface in console. default false but set true for gradual rollouts.
liam (infra): backwards compatibility: older runtimes should treat unknown fields as no-ops. default alias_mode=hard to preserve current semantics. we also need a migration path: enable soft-mode behind feature-flag per-cluster.
samir (runtime): +1 for feature-flag. also a small e2e test: script that flips an alias 50x in 5m and assert no >2x baseline cold starts.
vlad (sre): ops-bot create ticket INF-2026-78 for rollout metrics + alerting?
ops-bot: created INF-2026-78: "alias stability metrics + deferred eviction alerting" assigned to samir.
jess (arch): decision: prototype soft alias_mode + stability_window in staging. feature-flag rollout to canary clusters. samir to implement runtime lease states. liam to add migration toggle. nora to draft console copy and expected_behavior note. follow-up doc: RFC for alias lifecycle (link forthcoming).
liam (infra): i'll add a short config snippet for feature-flag gating.
nora (product): i'll coordinate with customer success about messaging. small follow-up: do we want a tenant override TTL so customers can opt-out?
jess (arch): yes — add `tenant_eviction_opt_out` boolean for enterprise tenants (requires auth). we'll capture in RFC.
vlad (sre): sounds good. leaving notes here for postmortem additions.
ops-bot: linked INF-2026-78 -> RFC-2026-12 (draft)
